newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ex-Tsumura head arrested for breach of trust -- NHK.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Tsumura head arrested for breach of trust -- NHK.

text.p: Prosecutors arrested the former president of Tsumura and Co and four other people on suspicion of breach of trust on Thursday, Japanese public television said.

NHK television said Akira Tsumura and the others were arrested for allegedly guaranteeing loans on Tsumura's part for the company's former subsidiary Tsumura Shoji without the consent of Tsumura's board.
Prosecutors declined to comment on the report of the arrest.
Tsumura is a Japanese company which makes Chinese herbal medicines.
Tsumura Shoji borrowed a total of five billion yen from some financial institutions in 1993 with the loan guarantees, NHK said.
Earlier on Thursday, prosecutors started searching the former president's home and some other places for evidence, NHK said.
The other four people arrested could not immediately be identified.
Tsumura officials were not immediately available for comment.
The Japanese economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Thursday that Tsumura Shoji's borrowings using loan guarantees totalled seven billion yen.
NHK said it was likely Tsumura Shoji borrowed an additional two billion yen from another financial institution in 1994, separately from the five billion yen of loans guaranteed in 1993.
Four billion yen worth of these loans to Tsumura Shoji appeared to have been used for real estate development projects and the amount is considered unrecoverable, NHK said.
Tsumura said on Wednesday that three banks had sought a court order demanding that Tsumura repay the loans which its former subsidiary obtained with the loan guarantees.
The three banks are Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd, Yasuda Trust & Banking Co Ltd and Kofuku Bank Ltd, a second-tier regional bank based in Osaka, western Japan, Tsumura said.
Tsumura said the banks' claims were not justifiable.
Nihon Keizai said Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co also extended loans to Tsumura Shoji.
